routes.description: Establish that life-permitting fine-tuning raises the probability of classical theism relative to the specified single-universe naturalistic alternatives.
routes.successCriteria: The likelihood and intrinsic-probability comparisons must jointly make fine-tuning substantially less expected under the relevant naturalistic space than under classical theism.

motionBridge.description: Show that fine-tuning provides strong comparative confirmation of classical theism over specified single-universe naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Establish that life-permitting parameters are substantially more expected given a perfectly good creator than given single-universe naturalism.
Show that naturalistic hypotheses augmented to predict fine-tuning occupy little relevant probability space despite their fit with the observation.
Establish that the coherence or simplicity of perfect-being theism preserves enough intrinsic probability to support the comparative inference.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why unrestricted naturalistic alternatives do not neutralize every possible empirical inference to theism.
Account for simulation and other naturalistic designer scenarios without merely relocating fine-tuning to an unexplained base reality.

routes.description: Undercut strong confirmation by challenging the likelihoods, hypothesis-space partition, intrinsic probabilities, and status of the fine-tuning datum.
routes.successCriteria: At least one indispensable comparative step must remain unjustified or sufficiently ambiguous that fine-tuning does not strongly discriminate in favor of God.

motionBridge.description: Show that fine-tuning does not securely yield strong comparative evidence for classical theism.

centralBridges.description: Challenge whether divine goodness supplies a justified prediction of a life-permitting or specifically fine-tuned universe.
Require comparison with the relevant naturalistic disjunction, including broad alien, simulation, and other naturalistic scenarios.
Challenge the assignment and aggregation of intrinsic probabilities across unlimited, limited, coherent, modest, and parsimonious hypotheses.
Show that competing theoretical virtues cannot be weighted precisely enough to support the asserted posterior comparison.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Preserve the possibility that apparently intentional phenomena receive unanticipated natural explanations.
Consider whether apparent fine-tuning indicates a defect of physical theory rather than an objective cosmic feature requiring design.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning as Data and the Theistic Likelihood
sections.rationale: The motion depends first on whether fine-tuning is an objective evidential datum and whether classical theism makes life-permitting conditions sufficiently expected.

sections.title: Scope and Granularity of the Comparison
sections.rationale: A comparative Bayesian inference requires a defined theistic hypothesis and a defined rival space whose members and level of specificity determine the relevant probabilities.

sections.title: Naturalistic Alternatives and Empirical Discrimination
sections.rationale: The force of fine-tuning evidence turns on whether available naturalistic auxiliaries legitimately diffuse the inference or instead generate unrestricted empirical skepticism.

sections.title: Agency, Motive, and Predictive Fit
sections.rationale: Evidence for intentional agency supports classical theism only if it also supplies justified information about the agent's goodness, purposes, and expected actions.

sections.title: Coherence, Modesty, and Intrinsic Probability
sections.rationale: The inference requires an account of how probability is distributed among perfect-being theism, limited alternatives, and naturalism augmented to predict fine-tuning.

sections.title: Parsimony and the Overall Probability Balance
sections.rationale: The motion-level conclusion requires integrating the claimed fine-tuning likelihood advantage with ontological parsimony and other theoretical virtues across the full comparison.
